messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@kinetichealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Kinetic Health — Go-live Readiness & Owner Playbook

Hi team,

We closed Kinetic Health yesterday (welcome onboard!) — quick handoff so CS and Implementation have the right context before the kickoff. High level:
- ACV: $420k annual commit (Reserved Dedicated cluster)
- Primary use: inference for clinical note summarization + embeddings for search
- Target go-live (customer-facing): 2027-04-15 (customer asked for aggressive ramp)
- Key constraints: HIPAA data handling, SSO with Okta, data residency: US only

Attached: mutual action plan, initial implementation scope, and the SOW draft. Please review the MAP and confirm owners and the 30/60/90 milestone split. My suggested plan:
  1) Discovery + security review (2/16–2/23)
  2) Integration & SSO (3/1–3/21)
  3) Staging & validation (3/22–4/5)
  4) Go-live prep & cutover (4/6–4/15)

Customer stakeholders (from last call): Jordan Ellis (Head of Product), Aaron Myers (Procurement), onboarding@kinetichealth.com.

Open items I flagged: SOC2 evidence request is pending; legal expects a few redlines in the SOW around liability and data processing. Also note they require a 99.9% regional latency SLA for the dedicated pool.

Ask: Marissa — can you own CS lead? Sofia — would you take program management/implementation owner? Vivek — please note the technical risks below and confirm prework we should ask Kinetic to schedule ahead of Discovery.

Thanks — I’ll stay on the thread for the initial coordination.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: RWI_mutual_action_plan_Kinetic.xlsx; Kinetic_implementation_scope_v1.pdf; SOW_RWI_Kinetic_v0.9.docx

Subject: Re: Kinetic Health — Go-live Readiness & Owner Playbook

Thanks Ben — congrats to the team for closing this. Quick acknowledgements and commitments from CS: 

Internal assignments (tentative):
- CS Lead: Marissa Cole — overall success plan, adoption, and executive syncs
- Implementation / PM: Sofia Ivanova — program schedule, milestones, resource coordination
- Solutions / SE: Vivek Kulkarni — technical design, staging validation, perf targets
- AE (handoff owner): Ben Carter — contract & billing handoffs, procurement follow-ups

Initial milestones (I refined Ben's suggestions):
- 2/16: Discovery (90m) — objectives: data flows, security checklist, SSO requirements; attendees: Jordan, Aaron, Kinetic infra lead + Redwood SE
- 2/18: Security questionnaire delivery — Kinetic to provide their baseline controls doc
- 2/23: Technical readiness sign-off — agree on firewall rules, IP allowlists, S3/GCS bucket policies
- 3/10: Internal performance baseline completed (small sample dataset)
- 3/22: Staging acceptance criteria review
- 4/6: Cutover window planning (backup rollback plan included)

Risks / blockers I've captured:
- Procurement has requested a 60-day SLA review period for license activation (Aaron)
- SOC2 evidence required before full dataset access; need legal callback on SOW redlines
- Customer expects private VPC deployment — confirm infra provisioning lead and timeline

Action items (owner | due):
- Ben: Share signed SOW and final billing contact (2/12)
- Jordan/Aaron (customer): Provide security contact + baseline controls doc (2/18)
- Vivek: Draft network/IP allowlist and expected ports for the staging cluster (2/15)
- Sofia: Build the internal project roster + kickoff calendar invite (2/12)

I’ll schedule the 2/16 discovery — Sofia, please include the SE checklist and invite the customer's SRE. Ben, loop in legal for the SOW redlines.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few technical notes from my side that will affect scheduling and the staging plan: 

1) Model & infra notes:
- We'll serve a fine-tuned LLM (3B parameter class) with quantized weights on dedicated GPU pool. Expected baseline throughput: 60 req/sec @ p95 latency target 280ms (token-limited). We should prototype with a 10k-document sample in staging for perf numbers.
- Embeddings workload will be batched; recommend enabling prefix caching for their query patterns to reduce token spend.

2) Data access & security:
- For HIPAA, we must ensure customer-managed keys (KMS) in their account or HSM key escrow. If they require our Private deployment in VPC, provisioning lead time is ~3 business days for infra + additional 5–7 days for network validation.
- SSO: we support SAML/OIDC (Okta preferred). We need an IdP metadata file and a test user before we can enable SP-initiated flows in staging.

3) Network / operations prework (items for 2/16 discovery):
- Customer to provide IP ranges for allowlisting and a temporary test token for initial integration
- Clarify whether logs can be exported to their SIEM (yes, but requires agreed retention window)

4) Blockers I see now:
- If legal requires limited data residency to a single region and also wants multi-zone failover, we need to clarify acceptable RTO/RPO constraints — that can affect cluster sizing and cost.

I'll attach a short SE checklist to use on the discovery call. Planning note: give me a heads-up 48 hours before discovery so I can reserve staging capacity.

- Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa / Sofia — thanks for the quick setup and the proposed milestones. Jordan here (Head of Product). Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- SSO / Okta: we can provide the IdP metadata and a test account by 2/15. Okta team is on standby but needs the SP details from your side.
- Data residency: we require all PHI to remain in a single US region but can accept cross-az failover; please confirm that logs containing PHI will not be sent outside our account.
- Timeline: 4/15 go-live is our target but our procurement lead (Aaron) asked whether a short pilot window in early April would be possible before full cutover. That would help our clinical ops validate downstream workflows.

We are happy to join the 2/16 discovery. Also: Ben, we uploaded the PO and signed cover page to your HubSpot attachment this morning.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Jordan Ellis
